goals.title: Establish maintained Pi orchestrator fork
goals.description: Maintain a full fork of the earendil-works/pi monorepo, keep main synchronized with upstream, maintain an orchestrator-compat branch, fix rpc-entry resolution and CLI packaging, and run compatibility smoke tests.

goals.title: Complete worker lifecycle monitoring
goals.description: Consume orchestrator events and status, detect completion and failure, expose live Pi UI updates, support cancellation and timeouts, and clean up worker processes deterministically.

goals.title: Implement bounded dependency-aware concurrency
goals.description: Launch two to four isolated workers from the ready queue, enforce dependency and concurrency limits, avoid duplicate dispatch, and schedule newly unblocked tasks deterministically.

goals.title: Validate and commit task work
goals.description: Inspect worker diffs, enforce task scope, run focused validation, reject unsafe output, create coherent conductor-owned commits, record evidence, and clean up completed task worktrees.

goals.title: Build deterministic sequential integration
goals.description: Integrate validated task commits in dependency order on the separate integration branch, refresh task bases after dependencies land, handle conflicts safely, and never merge into the user branch.

goals.title: Add independent review and repair passes
goals.description: Launch fresh reviewer agents for correctness, security, maintainability, tests, and documentation, prioritize findings, and apply important fixes through isolated repair attempts.

goals.title: Deliver final validation and merge-ready evidence
goals.description: Run the complete configured test and lint suite on the integration branch, verify repository cleanliness and history, and report the final branch, commits, reviews, tests, and remaining risks.

goals.title: Harden restart recovery and idempotency
goals.description: Add locked state transitions, schema migrations, daemon restart reconciliation, idempotent retries, orphan branch and worktree cleanup, and safe resume behavior across every run phase.

goals.title: Improve plan editing and approval experience
goals.description: Provide structured DAG visualization and editing, clear validation feedback, configurable worker limits, persisted plan revisions, and a concise final approval summary before side effects.

goals.title: Add run inspection and control commands
goals.description: Add commands and UI for listing runs, viewing task and attempt details, following worker output, retrying or cancelling work, pruning completed resources, and resuming interrupted runs.

goals.title: Expand end-to-end and fault-injection coverage
goals.description: Test real Pi and orchestrator workflows, concurrent scheduling, crashes at each state boundary, Git conflicts, worker failures, malformed state, cancellation, recovery, and platform-specific worktree behavior.

goals.title: Package release and CI automation
goals.description: Add GitHub Actions for checks and upstream compatibility, define versioning and release workflows, validate GitHub installation, prepare npm publication when appropriate, and document supported Pi and orchestrator versions.

goals.title: Define sandbox and permission policy
goals.description: Document the worker trust model, add optional sandbox integration, constrain credentials and destructive tools where possible, and make security boundaries explicit in prompts, configuration, and reports.

goals.title: Handle blocked worker prompts through typed RPC
goals.description: Detect Pi extension_ui_request events for select, confirm, input, and editor dialogs; expose blocked-worker state; send extension_ui_response through the worker RPC channel; apply a conservative configurable auto-cancel or decline policy; journal decisions; and add end-to-end tests for response, timeout, cancellation, and recovery behavior.

goals.title: Migrate compatibility fork to pi-server
goals.description: Synchronize the maintained Pi fork with upstream 0.81.1, migrate the orchestrator compatibility and worker security policy patches from packages/orchestrator to packages/server, update pi-build-conductor for PI_SERVER_DIR and server.sock, preserve ESM rpc-entry resolution, and run real server compatibility smoke tests.

goals.title: Integrate orchestration with pi-worklist
goals.description: Use a versioned pi.events capability protocol to select or provide a pi-worklist Project Goal, snapshot its exact revision, perform repository-aware planning, obtain explicit approval, create and atomically reconcile associated Session Task projections, consume structured user-override events, and degrade cleanly when pi-worklist is absent or incompatible. Execute the approved tasks as one orchestration session and write bounded status and result references back without automatically completing the Project Goal.

goals.title: Add repository-aware planning
goals.description: Give a read-only planning agent access to repository structure, instructions, manifests, conventions, relevant source files, and detected validation commands before it proposes an evidence-backed task DAG for approval.

goals.title: Generalize tasks into workflow steps
goals.description: Replace implementation-only task assumptions with typed investigation, change, command, and approval steps that declare dependencies, capabilities, path or resource locks, validation, outputs, timeouts, and retry policies.

goals.title: Make artifacts first-class outputs
goals.description: Persist typed reports, decisions, findings, test evidence, patches, commits, and merge candidates so dependent steps coordinate through explicit inspectable artifacts instead of only integrated Git changes.

goals.title: Build a reusable workflow engine
goals.description: Decompose the fixed BuildConductor lifecycle into a generic run state machine, scheduler, step handlers, executors, workspace providers, artifact storage, quality gates, event timelines, and conflict-aware resource scheduling.

goals.title: Provide built-in orchestration workflows
goals.description: Recast the current strict build lifecycle as a change workflow and add investigate and plan-only workflows while preserving approval, isolation, review, repair, validation, recovery, and evidence guarantees where applicable.

goals.title: Create zero-config repository onboarding
goals.description: Make /orchestrate usable directly in a normal repository, add optional initialization for persisted repository defaults under .pi, and explicitly support or document clean baselines, dirty worktrees, and repositories without an initial commit.

goals.title: Define generalized orchestration safety
goals.description: Preserve immutable approval and least-authority execution, introduce capability profiles for each step type, expose sandbox policy during approval, and keep deployment, publishing, cloud administration, and other external mutations disabled until safely supported.

goals.title: Rename and migrate the product surface
goals.description: Adopt neutral package, command, type, configuration, storage, and documentation naming centered on orchestration, provide /orchestrate as the main interface, and retain temporary /build aliases plus readers for existing run schemas.

goals.title: Prepare the generalized npm release
goals.description: Resolve the pinned server installation dependency, define a small supported public API or publish compiled JavaScript and declarations, finalize platform support, remove publication blockers, migrate existing users, and validate a complete clean-install orchestration flow before npm release.

goals.title: Add a headless orchestration CLI and structured output
goals.description: Publish a compiled CLI supporting bounded list and show operations, deterministic mutation results, stable typed errors, --json output, event streaming, and npm-installed execution without importing TypeScript from node_modules. Keep the Pi extension as an adapter over the same application service.

goals.title: Add pi-worklist compatibility and cross-extension E2E coverage
goals.description: Test capability negotiation, Project Goal intake, approved Session Task projections, user overrides, idempotent reconciliation, /tree, /fork, /clone, /resume, missing or incompatible pi-worklist versions, recovery, and the guarantee that the orchestrator never automatically completes a Project Goal.

goals.title: Add hierarchical roadmap planning
goals.description: Model a broad objective as an approved hierarchy of roadmap phases, repository runs, workflow steps, and attempts. Persist immutable roadmap revisions, phase outcomes, dependencies, success criteria, and evidence references while keeping detailed execution plans scoped to individual repository runs.

goals.title: Add multi-repository parent orchestration
goals.description: Coordinate a parent roadmap across multiple repositories while preserving independent repository policies, base snapshots, branches, worktrees, validation, merge candidates, recovery, and evidence. Track cross-repository dependencies through child-run and artifact references without combining repositories into one unsafe Git transaction.

goals.title: Materialize approved roadmaps into pi-worklist
goals.description: Convert an explicitly approved roadmap into idempotently created pi-worklist Project Goals carrying bounded roadmap and repository references. Negotiate the required capability through the versioned inter-extension protocol, never create or rewrite goals before approval, and never automatically complete a Project Goal.

goals.title: Add phase-boundary replanning
goals.description: After each roadmap phase, inspect current repository snapshots, consume produced artifacts and validation evidence, reassess remaining assumptions, and propose revisions to later phases. Require renewed approval whenever objectives, authority, mutation scope, validation commands, repository membership, or safety policy change.

goals.title: Add self-upgrade handoff and restart recovery
goals.description: When the orchestrator changes its own implementation, finish the current generation, persist a restart checkpoint, stop safely, load and verify the newly installed version, and resume through a new child run. Preserve schema and protocol compatibility and never hot-swap implementation code inside an active run.
